diffs.diff: header pin 19 (CS): part says power, datasheet reading says io
diffs.evidence: The LIS2HH12 datasheet (DocID025344, section 6) states 'To select/exploit the I2C interface, the CS line must be tied high (i.e. connected to Vdd_IO).', so in this I2C-only model CS is correctly wired to the 3.3 V supply (role power) rather than to a GPIO that would float at boot and could select SPI.

diffs.diff: header pin 22 (SDO): part says power, datasheet reading says io
diffs.evidence: The datasheet I2C section says 'If the SA0/SDO pin is connected to the supply voltage, the address is 0011101b' (0x1D), so in I2C mode SDO/SA0 is a static address strap that must not float; the model ties it to Vdd_IO (role power) to give address 0x1D, matching i2cAddress 29 and the driver default.

diffs.diff: acceleration (mg, FS ±2 g): datasheet reading gives 0.061 per count, the part's model has 0.000061, 0.000061, 0.000061
diffs.evidence: Equivalent units: Table 3 gives sensitivity '@ FS ±2.0 g 0.061 mg/digit' and the model's sim measures report X/Y/Z in g, so 0.061 mg/digit = 0.000061 g/digit, which is exactly the model's scale (the driver also uses 0.061 mg/digit divided by 1000).

diffs.diff: temperature (°C): datasheet reading gives 0.125 per count, the part's model has 0.000061, 0.000061, 0.000061
diffs.evidence: The datasheet Table 5 lists 'Temperature sensor output change' of 8 digit/°C (0.125 °C per count, agreeing with the second reading), but this model neither simulates nor drives the TEMP_L/TEMP_H registers; the three 0.000061 values the gate lists are the X/Y/Z acceleration channels, so there is no wrong temperature formula in the model.
